text: Rosa was chopping green onions when she remembered last night's match. She dried her hands and spoke to the kitchen speaker. "Excuse me, could you please read me the sports results from last night? I am cooking for my whole family, and my brother will ask about the score the moment he walks in, so I would like to know it before he does." The speaker understood that she wanted last night's sports results read aloud. It found the scores and began to deliver them in a calm voice. The home team had won by two goals. Rosa smiled and her whole body relaxed, because now she could tell her brother the news first. She went back to her onions with a happy hum.

Grandpa Leo could not sleep on Saturday night. At ten o'clock he picked up his phone and said, "Wake me at seven on Sunday, and let me stay in bed a little if I am tired." The phone understood that he wanted an alarm for seven in the morning with a snooze. It set the alarm for seven and a snooze of twenty minutes, and it told him so in a clear voice. Leo's feet felt frozen, so he pulled a thick blanket over them. He thanked the phone, put it on the table and closed his eyes. A few minutes later he was asleep.

Someone wants to know if the front door is locked.
Is the front door locked?
Check my front door, please.
Did I lock up?
I left in a hurry and now my phone is all I have. Is the door shut tight?
Tell me if the back door is locked too, and check the garage twice.
I will not earn any peace of mind unless I know the house is secure.
Be careful and look at every lock for me before I go to bed.
Is the door open or closed right now?
Could you please tell me whether the front door is locked, and if it is not, lock it?

Dana was packing lunches when her phone buzzed with an urgent news alert. "Read me the headlines about the bank loan rates," she said. Then she changed her mind. "No, sorry, I meant the local news, not the money news." The assistant understood the fix. It dropped the bank headlines and gave her three local stories instead: a road was closed near the school, a fair would be held on Saturday, and a new bus line would start next month. Dana listened while she cut the sandwiches in half. When it finished, she thanked the assistant and zipped up the lunch bags.

Walter burned his hand on the stove. He did not know what to do, and he was not good with his phone. He held it up and said, "Burn help." The assistant understood that he had a burn and wanted first aid steps. It told him to hold the burn under cool running water for ten minutes. Walter had a bag of frozen peas in the freezer and wanted to put them on his hand. The assistant said not to use ice or frozen things on a burn, and to bathe the burn in cool water instead. Walter did that, and the pain slowly got better. Then the assistant asked if he wanted to call a doctor.

Someone wants to join a video call.
Join my call.
Get me into the ten o'clock meeting.
Open the team call, please.
I'm in the car park buying milk and I'm late. Can you connect me to the meeting?
Start the call link from my calendar.
Put me in the call with the sound off.
Could you please join the budget meeting for me? I am about to lock my laptop and I would like to take the call on my phone, because my pricey headset is in my bag and I cannot reach it.
I need to be in the meeting in two minutes. Dial in now.

A bike route is a path from one place to another that is good for riding. People use routes to plan a ride, and many apps design one for you. You can change a route in simple ways. You can ask for a shorter ride, a flatter ride, or one with fewer big roads. You might say, "Plan a flat ride of ten miles," or "Keep me off the busy streets." During the ride you can ask, "How far have I gone?" or "How fast am I going?" Mia keeps a pencil note on her fridge with her best times. A crispy autumn morning is her favorite time to ride.

Someone wants to move a meeting to a later time.
Push my two o'clock to three.
Move the team meeting back an hour.
Can we do the dentist visit later in the day?
I am stuck in traffic and will miss my two o'clock.
Try to find a new time for the call, and send an update to everyone.
My afternoon is a mess. Could the meeting wait until tomorrow?
If you can, make the change automatic, so that the others are told right away.
Please shift my four o'clock meeting to five, as I have another thing on.

name: filter_check
does: Tells you if the air purifier filter needs to be wiped or replaced, so the whole house keeps clean air.
inputs: which purifier or room, and how long the filter has been in use
people say:
- Is my purifier filter still good?
- The air smells stale, does the filter need changing?
- My neighbor says a filter should be changed every three months. Is mine due?
- Does the machine in the bedroom need cleaning?
- When did I last change the filter downstairs?
- Tell me if the filter has gotten too dirty.

Person: Put a task on my list.
Assistant: What should the task say?
Person: Call the wifi company about the slow connection.
Assistant: Done. Do you want a due date?
Person: Yes, Friday. Actually, make it Thursday. I have too many things to do on Friday.
Assistant: I changed it to Thursday.
Person: Can you call them for me?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't make phone calls. I can remind you at nine on Thursday, if you like.
Person: Yes, please get me that reminder.

name: find_free_time
does: Looks through your calendar and finds a single free block of the length you want.
inputs: how long you need, and which days to look at
people say:
- When am I free this week for two hours?
- I need something to lift my week. Is there a quiet evening?
- Find me a single hour to listen to my audiobook.
- Do I have any gaps on Thursday?
- Where can I fit a long lunch with my sister?
- Show me when nothing is planned.

Person: I want to plan a dinner for the holiday.
Assistant: Which holiday, and how many people are coming?
Person: New Year's Eve. Six people. I just moved here, so I don't know anyone yet. These are my new neighbors.
Assistant: That sounds nice. Would you like a shopping list?
Person: Yes. We will make a toast at midnight, and everyone will be hungry by nine.
Assistant: I made a list with bread, cheese, juice and a cake. Anything else?
Person: Remind me tomorrow at seven to wash the good plates.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you tomorrow at seven.

Someone wants the living room to get warmer.
Warm up the living room.
Make it hotter in here.
Brr, it's cold.
Please turn the heat up to twenty-two degrees.
My toes are like ice. Can you do something about it?
Could you please warm up the living room fast? My hands hurt from the cold, and I want to sit down with a slice of melon and read.
Raise the temperature a few degrees.
I'm freezing, so get the radiator going.

name: leak_alert
does: Sends you a message when water is found where it should not be, so your home stays cozy and dry.
inputs: which room or pipe to watch, and who should get the message
people say:
- Is water leaking under the kitchen sink?
- I just got off the bus and I think the floor is wet at home.
- Something is dripping in the basement.
- Tell me right away if a pipe starts to leak.
- The ceiling has a damp spot. Is there a problem?

Priya stood by the open window, stirring soup, when her son shouted that he was hungry. She still had to make the rice. "Tell me how long to cook the rice and set a timer for it," she said to her phone. The assistant understood that she wanted two things. First it said that white rice takes about fifteen minutes. Then it set a timer for fifteen minutes and told her it had started. Priya had borrowed her neighbor's big pot, and she wanted to give it back clean. She smiled, turned down the heat, and wiped the table while the rice cooked.

Tom's uncle was mowing the lawn outside while Tom made pasta for the final dinner of the visit. His hands were full of flour, so he spoke to his phone. "Pasta time?" he asked. The assistant understood that he wanted to know how long to cook pasta. It said that dried spaghetti takes about ten minutes, and it offered to start a timer. Tom said yes. When the timer went off, the uncle came in with a green stain on his shoes, and the two of them sat down to eat.

name: first_aid_steps
does: Reads out simple steps for a small injury, one step at a time.
inputs: what happened, and where on the body it hurts
people say:
- I fell off my scooter and my knee is bleeding.
- Read me what to do for a cut.
- My finger got stuck in the door.
- What do I do when a bandage gets wet?
- My son has a scrape on his elbow. What now?
- How do I take care of a small burn?

Gus smelled smoke from burnt toast and gave up on cooking. He was tired and wanted to rest. He picked up his phone and typed, "order my usal pizza from luigis". The assistant understood that "usal" meant "usual". It found the pizza that Gus had ordered last time, a large one with mushrooms, and it asked him to confirm. Gus pressed yes. The assistant placed the order and said it would arrive in about thirty minutes. Gus opened a window to let the smoke out and sat down to wait.

Jo, a student, needed a haircut before her interview, but she had little money. She told her phone, "Book me a haircut for Saturday, and find a place that costs half as much as my last one." The assistant understood that she wanted a cheaper salon and a Saturday time. It looked at the shops nearby and found one that charged half the price. It booked ten o'clock on Saturday and put it on her calendar. Jo was also waiting for a parcel to ship, so she asked the assistant to move the haircut to the top of her list of things to do. It did, and she felt much better.

Ben was late for the bus, with a pot of soup still cooking at home and his bag half open. He pushed in his earbuds and said, "Keep my book going, but at one and a half speed, and tell me how many chapters are left." The assistant understood two things. It started the audiobook where he had stopped and made it play faster. Then it said that there were four chapters left. Ben was happy to hear that. He listened to the body of the story all the way to work, and he only remembered the soup when he got off the bus.

Someone wants to know when the recycling is collected.
When is bin day?
Is the recycling picked up this week?
The bin is full and the smell is bitter. Is it collection day soon?
I need to sort my trash before tomorrow. When do the trucks come?
Tell me which day the blue bin goes out.
The street looks empty of bins. Did I miss the pickup?
Could you please let me know when the next recycling collection is? My old toaster and a pile of boxes are in the hall.
What day do they take the paper?

Hiro was driving to work, stuck in traffic and bored. His nine o'clock call was about to start. He said to the car, "Join my nine o'clock call, but do not turn on the video." The assistant understood that he wanted to be in the call with his camera off. It dialed in and told him that he was connected with the video off. A coworker asked how his workout had gone, and Hiro began to talk about it. The cars started to move again, and he kept his eyes on the road.

Lena, a student, jumped out of bed and saw that it was bright outside. Her fish tank sat by the window, and she wanted some personal quiet to study. "Open the blinds halfway and close the curtains on the left window," she said. The assistant understood that she wanted both things done. It opened the blinds to the middle and closed the left curtains, and then it told her it was finished. The light fell on the tank, and the fish swam around. Lena opened her book and began to read.

Sam unlocked his car and sat down. He typed fast into his phone, "play the jazz stasion on the radio". To be safe, he waited until the car was parked and still before he sent it. The assistant understood that "stasion" meant "station". It found the jazz station and started to play it through the car speakers. His favorite band was on, and Sam turned up the sound a little. When he was ready to drive, he put the phone down and pulled out onto the road.

Mara owned a small shop, and a poster of a forest hung on its wall. One morning she heard a strange noise from the heater. She sighed a deep sigh and said to her phone, "Please book someone to fix the shop heater, and I want the same person who came twenty-five days ago." The assistant understood that she wanted a repair for the heater and the same worker as before. It looked at her past bookings and found his name. Then it booked him for Tuesday at noon. Mara asked if he could lift the heavy cover too, and the assistant added a note for him.

Ana had spent the day working in the garden. She had tied up the tomato plants and her back was sore. At night she said to her phone, "Wake me at six, but do not use the loud alarm. And don't let me forget to turn off the electric blanket." The assistant understood that she wanted a soft alarm and a reminder. It set a gentle wake-up sound for six in the morning, and it set a reminder to turn off the electric blanket at ten. Ana smiled, put her phone down and fell asleep quickly.

name: pool_care_helper
does: Tells you the pool's water temperature and what to do to keep it clean.
inputs: which pool or hot tub, and what you want to know
people say:
- Is the water warm enough to swim?
- Teach me how to cover the pool for the night.
- The kids dropped a juicy peach in the water. Is it dirty now?
- I need to buy chemicals at the pool store. What do I need?
- Why is the water cloudy?
- How hot is the hot tub right now?

Person: Make me a cup of tea.
Assistant: How strong would you like it?
Person: Strong. No wait, medium. My team of grandkids says I drink it too strong.
Assistant: Medium it is. Should I start it now?
Person: Yes. Can you plug in the kettle?
Assistant: I can't plug it in myself, but if the kettle is on a smart plug, I can switch it on. Is it?
Person: Yes, it is. Most mornings I use that one.
Assistant: Then I turned it on. Your tea will be ready in a few minutes.

Someone wants a reminder to do something later.
Remind me at six.
Let me know at six to start dinner and to turn off my audiobook.
Ping me when it's time for the bread.
Make sure I remember to call mom tonight and to pay the rent.
I want to be up bright and early, so nudge me at six tomorrow.
Could you please tell me at five to take the medicine, and remind me again an hour later?
Don't let me forget the meeting at ten.
When I get home, remind me to feed the cat.

Someone wants to change a measurement from one unit to another.
How many grams is a cup of flour?
Cups to grams, please.
The bakery scale shows ounces. What is that in grams?
Half a pound is how many ounces?
My recipe says a cup, but I only have a scale.
I don't want to pay for a wrong measurement, so tell me how many centimeters are in double this twelve inches.
Could you please change twenty degrees Celsius to Fahrenheit?
What is more, a kilo or two pounds?

Your files and folders hold your work on a computer. A file is one piece of work, like a letter or a photo, and a folder is a place where files are kept together. If the computer feels slow, it may have too many programs open, and restarting it often helps. People can also tag files with a word, like "school" or "bills", to find them again fast. When they want help, they say things like, "Open my tax folder," "Make the screen brighter," or "Restart the computer." They might ask, "How much battery is left?" or "Where did I put that file?"

Maya had just woken up and her head was still foggy. She looked at her phone and said, "Good morning. I am sorry to ask so early, but could you please look at my calendar and tell me what I have today? I have a new job, and I do not want to be late for my first meeting." The assistant understood that she wanted her day read to her. It began to search her calendar and found two events: a team meeting at nine and lunch with a friend at one. Maya sat up. She thanked the assistant and got out of bed.

someone wants to book a table at a restaurant.
book a table for four.
reserve me a spot for tonight at seven
i want a table outside in the fresh air, can you do that?
can you find somewhere delicious that is open late?
dont hide the menu from me, show me what they have, and book a tabel for two
get us seats at the pizza place on saturday
Could you please call the Thai restaurant and reserve a table for six people at eight tomorrow?
anything open near me with a free table now?

Kofi had just moved to the city and had little money. He sat at his kitchen table with a pile of bills. "Hello, could you please help me make a monthly budget? I just started a new job, and I have a hobby that costs a lot, so I want to see where my money goes." The assistant understood that he wanted to plan his spending. It asked how much he earned and then listed his rent, food and bills. Then it saw that the hobby took a big piece. Kofi looked at the numbers, took a deep breath, and tried to crack a smile. He felt that he could finally manage.

The news is a way to hear what is going on near you and around the world. Many people ask for headlines in the morning, or for the sports results. Some people want only local stories, and some want a certain topic, like weather, music or food. You can ask for fewer stories or for more. You can also block a topic you do not want to hear about. People say things like, "What's in the news?", "Read me the sports scores," or "Don't show me stories about celebrities." On a freezing morning, many people also ask if the roads are safe.

Mrs. Bell was not good with her phone. A message popped up that said the storage was full. She spoke to it. "Please help me. I need to make room for photos of my grandchildren." The assistant understood that she wanted to free up space. It looked through the phone and found twenty-five old videos that she had not opened for a year. It asked if she wanted to delete them, and she said yes. One was a video of a humid summer day at the beach, but she knew she had a plan to keep the photos safe. The assistant cleared the space, and Mrs. Bell smiled.

Jun was kneading dough when he remembered the bake sale. His hands were sticky, so he typed with one finger, "how long to let bred rise". The assistant understood that he meant bread. It said that bread dough rises for about an hour in a warm place, until it has doubled in size. Jun did not blink as he set a timer for sixty minutes. The bake sale was held monthly, and this time he wanted his loaves to be the best. He covered the bowl with a cloth and went for a walk while he waited.

Someone wants to check the spelling in a letter.
Spell check.
Check spelling.
Fix my typos.
Please look for mistakes in this message.
Is there anything wrong with the words I wrote? I'm tired.
Could you please read the page on my shelf of notes and tell me which words are spelled wrong?
Make my email short and crispy, and fix any spelling too.
I can wait while you look it over for errors.

Person: Good morning. Tell me how to make eggs.
Assistant: Good morning. How would you like them, fried, boiled or scrambled?
Person: Boiled. Hmm, I'm still half asleep. Make them scrambled, please. I want something to eat before the movie tonight.
Assistant: Scrambled it is. Crack two eggs into a bowl and stir them with a fork. Cook them on low heat.
Person: They look pale. Is that okay?
Assistant: Yes. Lift them with a spoon as they cook, and take them off when they are soft and just set.

A home security system helps you feel safe when you are away or asleep. It may have cameras, door sensors and an alarm. The cameras let you see who is at the door, and a motion sensor can tell you if someone moves in a room that should be empty. The idea is simple: you set it when you leave and turn it off when you come back. People use words like, "Turn on the alarm," "Show me the front door camera," or "Let me know if anything moves tonight." Some people ask the total number of times the door opened that day.

A workout is a plan for moving your body, and it is made of exercises. Each exercise is done in sets, and each set has a number of reps. For example, ten push-ups, then a rest, then ten more is two sets. Rest days are also important, because muscles need time to grow. People change workouts by making them longer, shorter, easier or harder. They say, "Give me a short workout," "Add another set," or "Explain this exercise again." My brother likes to train early, when the sky is still dark, and he always asks what comes next.

A podcast is a show that comes in episodes, and an audiobook is a book that is read to you in chapters. Your device remembers where you left off, so you can start again later. Many people change the playback speed, so a show goes faster or slower. They say things like, "Play the next episode," "Skip back thirty seconds," or "Go back to where I was." Some people listen while they clean the carpet or while a roast cooks in the oven. If a show does not work well, you can ask to go to another one.

Kim, a student, was nervous about a call with her cousin in Tokyo. She tied her scarf around her neck and pointed at the clock on her phone. "What time is it in Tokyo, and when should I call so it is not too late for her?" she asked. The assistant understood that she wanted two things. First it said that it was three in the afternoon in Kim's town, and eight the next morning in Tokyo. Then it said that a call at seven in the evening would be a good time. Kim thanked it and felt less nervous.

Someone wants to know how long to bake a chicken.
how long for chicken in the oven
what temp for a whole chicken?
I want to win dinner tonight. How long do I roast a chicken?
when will my chiken be done?
Tell me the time and the heat for a chicken, and what to serve as a snack.
Could you please tell me how long to cook a chicken? My family only does this big meal yearly, and I want it to be right.
Give me the oven steps for a roast chicken.

Grandma Ruth came home from the store in the van and felt hot and tired. The house was freezing in winter, but in summer it was like an oven. "Turn on the fan in the living room and tell me when it is cool enough to open the windows," she said to the speaker. The assistant understood that she wanted two things. It switched on the fan, and it checked the room's temperature. When the room reached twenty-three degrees, it told her. Ruth sat down with a glass of water and let the cool air return to the room.

Grandpa Joe sat at his desk with a cup of bitter coffee. He needed to send an invoice to a customer before the meeting. "Open the video call for ten o'clock and show me my last invoice," he said to the tablet. The assistant understood that he wanted two things. It opened the call link, and it put the last invoice on the screen. Joe checked the numbers and pressed send. When the meeting began, he said thank you to everyone for joining. The call went well, and he finished his coffee.

Gus, a gardener, wanted to see a dentist. He said to his phone, "Book me with Dr. Lee on Monday at ten." Then he looked at his window and saw the rain. "No, wait, Tuesday. I have a long job on Monday." The assistant understood that he wanted to fix the day. It changed the booking to Tuesday at ten and repeated the details back to him: Dr. Lee, Tuesday, ten o'clock. Gus said that was right. He put on his boots and went out to water the plants.

Mr. Park was a retired teacher who liked to bake. He had a jog planned for the morning and wanted to make his favorite cake after. "Tell me how long the cake takes, but I don't want the recipe with nuts," he said to the speaker. The assistant understood that he wanted the baking time and a cake without nuts. It said that a plain sponge cake takes about thirty-five minutes at one hundred and eighty degrees. It did not read the nut recipe. Mr. Park said that he would take care to turn the oven on after his jog.

Nina was eight, and she was hungry. Her mom was out, and the kitchen was closed to her except for the table. She wore her old jeans and held her tablet in both hands. She typed fast, "how do i maek toast". The assistant understood that she wanted to make toast. It told her in simple steps to ask a grown-up to help with the toaster. Nina wanted to train to be a good cook one day, so she watched. Her dad came in and put the bread in. Soon it popped up, and Nina spread jam on it.

name: unread_mail_reader
does: Reads out the unread messages in your inbox, starting with the newest.
inputs: how many messages to read, and who they are from if you want only some
people say:
- Did anyone write to me this morning?
- Read me the email from the man about the hedge.
- Do I have new mail?
- What came in while I was out?
- Show me the black marked messages first.
